title: "R Hands-on Workshop Series"
subtitle: "Data analysis in R with the tidyverse, built on base R foundations — from messy raw data to tables and plots"
toc: false
---

Welcome! This hands-on workshop teaches you to analyze data in **R** using the **tidyverse**, and the **base R** foundations underneath it: vectors, types, subsetting, lists, and functions. Each lesson also shows the base R version of key tidyverse steps, so you can read other people's code (see [Base R ↔ tidyverse](pages/base-vs-tidyverse.qmd)). You will take a realistic, messy outbreak dataset all the way from the raw file to clean data, summary tables, and publication-ready plots — and finish by writing your own functions and loops.

No experience with R or programming is needed.

## What you'll learn

-   Set up a project folder and import data from almost any file type
-   Inspect a dataset and find its problems before you analyze it
-   Clean messy data: fix column names, types, misspellings, impossible values, and duplicates
-   Handle missing values and join datasets together
-   Understand how R stores data (vectors, lists, data frames), and reshape it between wide and long
-   Read base R code and translate it to the tidyverse (and back)
-   Summarize data and make a publication-ready "Table 1"
-   Make histograms, scatter plots, box plots, bar charts, and epidemic curves with **ggplot2**
-   Write your own functions and loops to automate repeated work

## Start here

1.  **[Setup](pages/setup.qmd)** — install R, Positron, and the packages, and download the workshop folder. Please do this **before** the first session.
2.  **Work through the lessons in order:**

::: lesson-list
| \#    | Lesson                                                                   | You will learn                                                                  |
|-------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 1     | [Setup and a first look at your data](pages/lessons/01-setup-and-first-look.qmd) | R basics, packages, project folders, importing and inspecting data       |
| 2     | [Cleaning](pages/lessons/02-cleaning.qmd)                                                 | the pipe `%>%`, `clean_names()`, `mutate()`, `if_else()`, `case_when()`          |
| 3     | [Missing data, joins, and export](pages/lessons/03-missing-data-joins-export.qmd)                          | missing values, duplicates, joins, `export()`                                   |
| 4     | [Data structures](pages/lessons/04-data-structures.qmd)                                          | vectors, subsetting, lists, `pivot_longer()` / `pivot_wider()`                  |
| 5     | [Summarizing](pages/lessons/05-summarizing.qmd)                                              | `count()`, `summarise()`, `tabyl()`, a `gtsummary` Table 1                      |
| 6     | [Plotting basics](pages/lessons/06-plotting-basics.qmd)                                          | histograms, scatter plots, box plots                                            |
| 7     | [Plotting further](pages/lessons/07-plotting-further.qmd)                                         | bar charts, colors, epidemic curves, facets                                     |
| 8     | [Programming](pages/lessons/08-programming.qmd) *(optional)*                                    | functions, `if`/`else`, loops, `map()`                                          |
:::

## How each lesson works

Every lesson is split into short parts. Each part follows the same rhythm:

-   **👀 Follow along** — the instructor live-codes a new skill on the workshop dataset, and you type the same code into your **student script** (download it from the top of each lesson).
-   **✏️ TRY IT** — straight away, you do the same thing yourself on a practice dataset (a measles outbreak). Each TRY IT has a ✅ **Check** so you know whether you got it right, and a **solution** you can open if you're stuck.

During live sessions, put up your **green sticky note** when you finish a TRY IT, or your **red** one if you need help.

::: callout-tip
## Learning on your own?

You can! Each lesson page has everything you need: the explanations, the code with its output, every TRY IT, and its solution. Download the student script and work through the page at your own pace.
:::
